calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Intro
calls.summary: Federico Maffei (OpenTable senior engineering manager) met with Daniel Wathne and Logan (GrowthBook) to discuss replacing their aging, internally-built A/B testing tool. Key pain points included a clunky frontend, inability to run tests beyond two weeks, disconnected feature flags, and reliance on a shrinking maintenance team. Next steps involve Federico sharing detailed requirements, followed by a larger demo on Thursday with OpenTable’s cross-functional working group, and potentially a tailored trial.

calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Intro/Recap
calls.summary: GrowthBook demonstrated its feature flag and experimentation platform to OpenTable, highlighting the ability to replace OpenTable's aging internal tool by addressing key pain points like poor self-service UX, reliance on Mixpanel for real-time data, and frequent experiment configuration errors. Key participants included GrowthBook’s sales lead Daniel, solutions engineer Logan, and CEO Graham, while OpenTable was represented by product engineering lead Justin, senior engineering director Chris, and engineer Federico. Next steps involve scoping a proof of concept, aligning on timelines, and potentially completing a security review.

calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: Federico Maffei (OpenTable engineering manager) and Daniel Wathne (GrowthBook sales) discussed replacing OpenTable’s internal experimentation tool with GrowthBook, addressing pain points around scalability, friction, and StatSig’s instability due to its acquisition by Amplitude. Federico is convinced but needs to persuade the data analytics team, which is also considering StatSig. Next steps: Daniel will prepare a pricing proposal and ROI deck for Federico to present to executives next Thursday, with a follow-up meeting scheduled for Tuesday to review numbers and possibly include key stakeholders.

calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Check in
calls.summary: In the call, Federico Maffei (OpenTable's product lead) informed Daniel Wathne (GrowthBook) that OpenTable's execs are aligned on GrowthBook’s feature set and pricing, with key pain points around Statsig's pricing uncertainty and the data team’s resource constraints for a proof of concept (POC). Federico is handing off to Chris (his manager) and Forest (senior data analytics lead), who will drive the evaluation. Next steps: Daniel will schedule a meeting next Tuesday with Chris, Forest, and engineer Rahul to scope a two-month POC (June–July), with a possible smaller initial contract to ease the data team’s workload.

calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Check In - POC Sync
calls.summary: The meeting addressed the need to extend the POC period to at least a quarter due to the complexity of setup, data integration, and vendor onboarding. Key phases include environment setup, historical data replay, and backend testing. Participants highlighted that internal approval delays, especially in legal and security reviews, are critical blockers. GrowthBook will provide necessary documentation to facilitate onboarding, and discussions on Snowflake integration were crucial for validating the stats engine. Regular check-ins and open communication were emphasized to enhance collaboration and manage risks effectively, with teams aligning on expectations and timelines.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Opentable - Check In
calls.summary: The team is nearing completion of the security and procurement reviews, with key approvals pending to initiate the POC. Lydia is leading the third-party cyber risk assessment while the SOC 2 audit is finishing, essential for advancing onboarding. Stalled onboarding is due to final sign-offs and internal security reviews, with efforts from Federico and collaboration with Rahul's team crucial for POC success. Leadership has endorsed moving forward, reducing risks associated with onboarding delays, while Federico aims to proactively engage stakeholders to accelerate progress. The timing for contract finalization is affected by the quarter-end, but aims for execution by late August or early September remain realistic, emphasizing the need for clear communication to maintain momentum.

calls.title: Growthbook <> OpenTable - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The discussion centered on contract negotiation and pricing strategies, with the aim of concluding the agreement by the end of Q3. Key points included significant discounts on the platform fee and seat costs, allowing flexibility for seat additions. Participants highlighted the importance of synchronizing legal reviews with internal agreements to facilitate timely onboarding, while also discussing the enhancement of the Proof of Concept (PoC) beyond an initial month. Security requirements and technical dependencies were flagged as potential blockers, necessitating early attention. The overarching goal is to create a stable long-term partnership, emphasizing predictable pricing and timely decision-making to ensure a smooth transition into Q4.
